stem:
A 60-year-old man with advanced cirrhosis develops generalized edema and a low plasma oncotic pressure.

Synthesis of which of the following plasma proteins — the most abundant in plasma — is most impaired by his failing liver?

options.label: A
options.misconception: Antibodies are being treated as the dominant liver-made protein.
options.explanation: Immunoglobulins are secreted by plasma cells (differentiated B lymphocytes), not by hepatocytes, and are far less abundant than albumin.

options.label: B
options.misconception: None; albumin is the liver-made protein that dominates plasma.
options.explanation: Albumin is the most abundant of the plasma proteins and is manufactured by the liver; failing hepatic synthesis lowers plasma oncotic pressure and produces edema.

options.label: C
options.misconception: A clotting protein is being confused with the oncotic protein.
options.explanation: Fibrinogen is indeed liver-made, but its deficiency causes bleeding rather than edema; the most abundant plasma protein, which maintains oncotic pressure, is albumin.

options.label: D
options.misconception: An intracellular red-cell protein is being counted as a plasma protein.
options.explanation: Hemoglobin is packaged inside erythrocytes and is not a plasma protein at all; the dominant dissolved plasma protein is albumin.

options.label: E
options.misconception: A trace transport protein is being elevated to the most abundant.
options.explanation: Transferrin carries iron in small quantities; albumin far outweighs it in plasma and supplies most of the oncotic pressure lost in liver failure.

context: Learning objective: rank the plasma proteins. About 7 percent of plasma volume is protein, dominated by three liver-made groups — albumin, globulins, and fibrinogen. Albumin is the most abundant and is the principal determinant of plasma oncotic pressure, which is why cirrhosis causes edema.
